rules: only sources opened in this session (url_opened); numbers copied from opened abstract/PDF text or UNKNOWN; no market data fetched

entries.title: The Crypto Carry Trade
entries.authors: Nicolas Christin; Bryan R. Routledge; Kyle Soska; Ariel Zetlin-Jones
entries.venue: Carnegie Mellon University working paper (version 1.0, 1 Aug 2022)
entries.mechanism: short perpetual + long spot earns funding paid by a leverage-seeking long side (funding carry)
entries.market: Binance perpetual futures (USDT-settled and BTC/coin-settled contracts) vs spot
entries.period: sample includes H1 2021 heavy-volume period; exact start/end not extracted (UNKNOWN)
entries.universe: BTC plus 17 further coins, each with a USDT-settled and a coin-settled perpetual
entries.effect_size: in-sample annual Sharpe ratios 7 to 10 (abstract); BTC contracts 12.8 and 7.0 (introduction)
entries.effect_unit_horizon: annualised Sharpe ratio of 8-hour funding-window returns
entries.costs_included: no (paper abstracts from margin, leverage and transaction costs)
entries.capacity_notes: not addressed; exchange/counterparty risk discussed qualitatively
entries.notes: USDT-settled leg is in our forward USDT-M collection; coin-settled leg is COIN-M (BLOCKED_UNTIL_2026-11-28). Authors report carry returns lower for coin-settled than USDT-settled contracts. Sharpe inflated by low funding volatility; not a net trading result.

entries.title: Perpetual Futures Pricing
entries.authors: Damien Ackerer; Julien Hugonnier; Urban Jermann
entries.mechanism: no-arbitrage pricing of linear, inverse and quanto perpetuals; perp price = risk-neutral expected spot at a random time set by anchoring intensity
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN
entries.notes: Shows funding specifications under which perp and spot coincide and replication is possible. Theory anchor for basis/funding link.

entries.title: Cryptocurrency as an Investable Asset Class: Coming of Age
entries.authors: Nicola Borri; Yukun Liu; Aleh Tsyvinski; Xi Wu
entries.mechanism: survey of seven stylized facts; fact 6: crypto carry (short perp, long spot, per Schmeling et al.) compressed since 2024
entries.market: crypto perpetuals vs spot (Tether carry as in Schmeling, Schrimpf & Todorov)
entries.universe: UNKNOWN (carry construction follows Schmeling et al.)
entries.effect_size: carry annualised Sharpe 6.45 full sample; 4.06 from 2024; negative in 2025; funding mean return about 8% with volatility 0.8%
entries.gross_or_net: UNKNOWN (not stated in the extracted section)
entries.notes: Independent confirmation that carry level decayed post-2024; consistent with RESULTS_carry_v1.md (edge shrank below costs).

entries.title: Econometric Analysis of Cryptocurrency Markets: A Time Series Approach
entries.authors: Emre Inan
entries.mechanism: time-series predictability of BTC perpetual funding rates (double autoregressive models)
entries.market: Bitcoin perpetual futures, several exchanges (not named in abstract)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: predictability exists and varies over time and across exchanges)
entries.effect_unit_horizon: one-step-ahead out-of-sample point forecast of funding rate
entries.notes: Funding persistence = forecastability of the carry cash-flow, not of price. Not peer-reviewed.

entries.title: Can Funding Rate Predict Price Change?
entries.authors: Jin H. Jung (Presto Research)
entries.mechanism: funding change vs price change (contemporaneous and predictive), single asset and cross-section
entries.market: Binance BTC perpetual; Binance USDT-M top 50 for cross-sectional signal
entries.effect_size: contemporaneous R2 12.5% (7-day funding change vs 7-day price change); predictive R2 approx. 0 for BTC; cross-sectional result described only qualitatively
entries.costs_included: no (cross-sectional test explicitly without transaction costs; very high turnover)
entries.notes: Claims only. Supports lab finding in studies/FUNDING_m21h.md that funding adds no single-asset directional information.

entries.title: Crypto Carry: The Funding-Rate Cross-Section, Net of Costs and the Liquidation Tail (Alpha Research, Paper 2)
entries.authors: Bryan Vine
entries.mechanism: funding level harvest (cash-and-carry) vs dollar-neutral cross-sectional funding factor
entries.market: 30 Binance USD-M perpetuals with daily spot
entries.effect_size: cash-and-carry net about +5.6%/yr full sample, negative in 2026; cross-sectional factor Sharpe 0.90 gross, 0.71 net in-sample, 0.39 net OOS; rank IC funding vs fwd 7d return -0.005 (t -0.89); PBO 0.81
entries.effect_unit_horizon: annual return / annualised Sharpe; weekly rebalance; 7-day forward return
entries.costs_included: cross-section: 6 bp per side (swept 0-15 bp); carry: round-trip cost per entry, figure not given
entries.capacity_notes: not addressed; spot used as proxy for perp prices
entries.notes: Claims only, unreviewed. High PBO by the author's own measure; treat net figures as weak. Lab's carry family (F1 fcarry) is the same-asset hedged version.

entries.title: Three essays on futures expected returns: from dated futures to perpetual futures
entries.authors: Pengfei Luo
entries.venue: University of Edinburgh thesis (Edinburgh Research Archive, 2025-06-25)
entries.mechanism: cost-of-carry model for perpetuals; cross-sectional return predictors; category momentum
entries.effect_size: 170 predictors tested, 63 significant at 5%; all 63 explained by a two-factor (log-basis + price-volume) model; numerical returns UNKNOWN
entries.notes: Closest verified match for the director's lead 'Anatomy of cryptocurrency perpetual futures returns' (exact title not found; see unverified leads). Same 170/63 numbers as Cao et al. SSRN 6365329 cited in NEXT_MECHANISMS.md row J (rejected: multiple testing, overlaps carry/momentum).

entries.title: Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures
entries.authors: Songrun He; Asaf Manela; Omri Ross; Victor von Wachter
entries.mechanism: random-maturity no-arbitrage bounds for perps; deviation of perp from spot (annualised) and convergence trade
entries.market: crypto perpetuals vs spot (Binance cost tiers; Kaiko order-book sample)
entries.effect_size: mean absolute deviation about 60-90% per year; BTC arbitrage Sharpe 1.8 under high retail trading costs, up to 3.5 for zero-fee market makers; |deviation| shrinks about 11% per year
entries.effect_unit_horizon: annualised deviation (percentage points); annualised Sharpe of threshold strategy
entries.costs_included: yes, fee tiers (Binance) in bounds; margin/funding-of-capital treatment UNKNOWN
entries.capacity_notes: paper notes Sharpe stays above traditional markets when strategy scales; capacity numbers UNKNOWN
entries.notes: Strongest perp-specific evidence with costs. Deviations decline over time: pre-2022-heavy sample. Lab analogue: perp_premium_convergence (scanner_premium lanes, PREMIUM_BANER_REKONSTRUKTION).

entries.title: Crypto carry
entries.authors: Maik Schmeling; Andreas Schrimpf; Karamfil Todorov
entries.mechanism: futures-spot carry driven by volatile convenience yield: trend-chasing small investors vs scarce arbitrage capital
entries.market: crypto futures (perpetual and dated) vs spot
entries.effect_size: carry up to 60% p.a., strongly time-varying; averages above 10% annually (contribution section); high carry predicts future crashes (no number on page)
entries.gross_or_net: gross (carry level, not a trading P&L)
entries.capacity_notes: arbitrage capital scarce; margin spikes and liquidations make cash-and-carry risky
entries.notes: Published version reportedly in Management Science (doi 10.1287/mnsc.2024.05069; page returned 403, not verified). Dated-futures leg on Binance is partly COIN-M (blocked until 11-28).

entries.title: Perpetual Futures and Basis Risk: Evidence from Cryptocurrency
entries.authors: Will Gornall; Martin Rinaldi; Yizhou Xiao
entries.venue: preliminary working paper, 19 May 2025 (AEA 2026 conference program)
entries.mechanism: perpetual design (frequent small funding) vs quarterly futures; capital-constrained arbitrage
entries.market: crypto perpetual and quarterly futures (BitMEX example)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: perps dominate volume, enhance liquidity, reduce extreme dislocations and arbitrage drawdowns)
entries.capacity_notes: arbitrage drawdowns lower with perps than with dated futures
entries.notes: Quarterly futures comparison needs dated contracts; Binance dated USD-M exist (F2 dbasis), coin-margined dated contracts are COIN-M (blocked to 11-28).

entries.title: Cryptocurrency anomalies and economic constraints
entries.authors: Christian Fieberg; Gerrit Liedtke; Adam Zaremba
entries.mechanism: published crypto anomalies (size, volume, momentum, etc.) re-tested under economic constraints (micro-caps, costs, short side)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract gives no numbers): size/volume anomalies come from micro-caps; momentum survives in larger coins but with substantial trading costs, alpha mostly from shorts; abnormal returns concentrated in bull markets and fading over time
entries.oos_or_replication: re-test of published anomalies; decay over time
entries.notes: Director's named starting point. ScienceDirect and open.icm.edu.pl returned 403; verified via IDEAS/RePEc abstract page. Key negative evidence: anomalies mostly not tradable after constraints.

entries.title: Risks and Returns of Cryptocurrency
entries.authors: Yukun Liu; Aleh Tsyvinski
entries.mechanism: crypto-specific factors: time-series momentum, investor attention, network adoption
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: strong time-series momentum; attention proxies strongly forecast returns)
entries.notes: NBER page summary listed Itay Goldstein as co-author; EconPapers shows he is the RFS editor. Lab's tsmom_v1 failed on power (RESULTS_tsmom_v1.md).

entries.title: Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency
entries.authors: Yukun Liu; Aleh Tsyvinski; Xi Wu
entries.mechanism: three-factor model: market, size, momentum
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: nine long-short strategies with significant excess returns, all spanned by 3 factors)
entries.effect_unit_horizon: UNKNOWN (weekly portfolios per paper body, not verified)
entries.notes: Fieberg et al. (E01) and Ammann et al. (E22) challenge tradability/robustness of these factors.

entries.title: Cryptocurrencies and momentum
entries.authors: Klaus Grobys; Niranjan Sapkota
entries.mechanism: cross-sectional (and time-series) momentum
entries.effect_size: no significant momentum payoffs (abstract)
entries.notes: Contradicts Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu; small, early, pre-2019 sample.

entries.title: Momentum Trading in Cryptocurrencies: A Comparative Study of Time-Series and Cross-Sectional Strategies
entries.authors: Adedeji Daniel Gbadebo
entries.mechanism: multi-horizon EMA time-series momentum with volatility normalisation vs cross-sectional ranking
entries.universe: 8 coins: BTC, ETH, LTC, XRP, BNB, ADA, DOGE, SOL
entries.effect_size: TSMOM 31.96% annual return; XSMOM max drawdown 55.0% and lower returns
entries.notes: Small universe, low-ranked venue, single sample; no buy-and-hold benchmark comparison visible in abstract.

entries.title: Momentum and liquidity in cryptocurrencies
entries.authors: Stjepan Begusic; Zvonko Kostanjcar
entries.mechanism: double sorts on momentum and liquidity; momentum strongest in the most liquid coins (herding)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: strong momentum in most liquid coins; long-only 'illiquid losers' and 'liquid winners' beat cap-weighted on risk-adjusted basis)
entries.notes: Supports the liquidity split momentum (liquid) vs reversal (illiquid) seen in E14/E15.

entries.title: In Crypto We Trend
entries.authors: Andre Rzym; Tarek Abou Zeid (Man Group / Man AHL)
entries.mechanism: moving-average and breakout trend following with volatility scaling across coins
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (Sharpe described as higher than expected, no figure); average pairwise high-frequency correlation about 0.6
entries.gross_or_net: net (states transaction costs, shorting costs, liquidity constraints included)
entries.capacity_notes: liquidity ample for top 15, falls sharply beyond
entries.notes: Claims only. Correlation 0.6 matches lab power concern (DONCHIAN_POWER_P1: 20 coins ~1.5 independent at rho 0.65).

entries.title: Up or down? Short-term reversal, momentum, and liquidity effects in cryptocurrency markets
entries.authors: Adam Zaremba; Mehmet Huseyin Bilgin; Huaigang Long; Aleksander Mercik; Jan J. Szczygielski
entries.mechanism: daily short-term reversal driven by illiquidity; daily momentum in the largest coins
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: low last-day return coins significantly outperform high last-day return coins)
entries.capacity_notes: effect located in illiquid coins = low capacity
entries.notes: Horizon/liquidity split: reversal in illiquid, momentum in largest. Lab universe (liquid USDT-M perps) sits on the momentum side.

entries.title: Impact of size and volume on cryptocurrency momentum and reversal
entries.authors: Milan Ficura
entries.venue: FFA Working Papers 5:003 (Prague University of Economics and Business)
entries.mechanism: weekly reversal in small/illiquid coins, weekly momentum in large/liquid; distance to k-week high
entries.effect_size: weekly reversal small/illiquid t=-7.31; weekly momentum large/liquid t=2.33; distance to 1-week high t=-9.03 (small) / t=4.93 (large)
entries.notes: Only t-stats reported on page; no return magnitudes. Links to VOCABULARY anchoring_to_high (catalogue, untested).

entries.title: Two-Regime Liquidity Recovery After a Perpetual Futures Liquidation Cascade: Evidence from Hyperliquid and the October 10, 2025 Event
entries.authors: Boon Chuan Lim
entries.venue: The Journal of FinTech and Digital Assets 1(2):54-68
entries.mechanism: liquidity (spread vs depth) recovery after a liquidation cascade
entries.effect_size: pooled median quoted spread peaked 9.4 bp (p95 87.5 bp); spreads back within 1.2x pre-event within 23 days; depth ended at 66-79% of pre-event for 4 of 5
entries.notes: Single event, new venue/journal, independent author. Price reversal not studied: cost side only.

entries.title: How to measure the liquidity of cryptocurrency markets?
entries.authors: Alexander Brauneis; Roland Mestel; Ryan Riordan; Erik Theissen
entries.mechanism: validation of low-frequency liquidity proxies against order-book benchmarks
entries.market: BTC and ETH on Bitfinex, Bitstamp, Coinbase Pro
entries.effect_size: n/a: Corwin-Schultz and Abdi-Ranaldo best for time variation; Kyle-Obizhaeva and Amihud best for levels and venue ranking
entries.notes: Methodological: which proxy to trust when only klines exist (relevant for historical cost estimates after 11-14).

entries.title: Microstructure and Market Dynamics in Crypto Markets
entries.authors: David Easley; Maureen O'Hara; Songshan Yang; Zhibai Zhang
entries.mechanism: microstructure measures (Roll, VPIN, etc.) as ML predictors of price dynamics
entries.period: per search summary Jan 2021 - Jul 2023 (not verified in extracted text)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: predictive power for dynamics relevant to market making, hedging and volatility estimation; stable in crypto winter)
entries.notes: Predicts dynamics (volatility, spreads, etc.), not a trading P&L.

entries.title: The Quarter-Hour Effect: Periodic Algorithmic Trading and Return Predictability in Cryptocurrency Futures
entries.authors: Chan Kim; Peter Reinhard Hansen
entries.mechanism: clock-time algorithmic bursts; order imbalance at quarter-hour openings
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: quarter-hour opening imbalance forecasts 4-12 hour returns; opening returns predictable out of sample; 1- and 5-minute marks weak)
entries.notes: Already listed in studies/ONLINE_EDGES_2026-11-05.md section 7. Needs trade-level (aggTrades) forward collection; check collector coverage. Very recent, unreplicated.

entries.title: Market Reaction to Exchange Listings of Cryptocurrencies
entries.authors: Lennart Ante
entries.venue: Blockchain Research Lab Working Paper No. 3
entries.mechanism: event study of exchange listings
entries.effect_size: average abnormal return 5.7% on listing day; 9.2% over [-3,+3] days; up to 25.5% on some exchanges; some exchanges negative
entries.capacity_notes: pre-listing run-up and informed trading suggested
entries.notes: Pre-2019. Announcement reaction = speed race (NEXT_MECHANISMS row H rejected). Lab measures listing funding (H4/H5/H5F) not returns.

entries.title: Cryptocurrency Exchange Listings (Extended Abstract)
entries.authors: Jiasun Li; Mei Luo; Muzhi Wang; Zhe Wei
entries.venue: AFT 2025, LIPIcs vol. 354, paper 11 (full version SSRN 4715718)
entries.mechanism: listing returns and exchange incentives (VC-arm conflicts, regulation)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN on opened page (positive short-run abnormal returns on both, significantly larger on Coinbase); search snippet of slides gave first-day 32.8% vs 22.7% - NOT verified
entries.notes: Binance self-invested listings have weaker fundamentals (abstract). Relevant to H5F/M1F forward listing/monitoring tests.

entries.title: Survivorship and Delisting Bias in Cryptocurrency Markets
entries.authors: Manuel Ammann; Luca Liebi; Tom Burdorf; Sebastian Stoeckl
entries.mechanism: survivorship/delisting bias in crypto return samples
entries.effect_size: annualised survivorship bias 0.93% (value-weighted) and 62.19% (equal-weighted); size premium inflated; no positive return relation to momentum or beta after correction
entries.notes: Directly contradicts momentum premium once survivorship corrected. Supports FACTORY_SECURITY point-in-time universe rule.

entries.title: Crypto Wash Trading
entries.authors: Lin William Cong; Xi Li; Ke Tang; Yang Yang
entries.mechanism: fabricated volume on unregulated exchanges (Benford, rounding, tail tests)
entries.effect_size: wash trading averages over 70% of reported volume on unregulated exchanges
entries.notes: Data-quality caveat for any volume-based signal or venue ranking; regulated venues looked normal.

entries.title: Return and Volatility Forecasting Using On-Chain Flows in Cryptocurrency Markets
entries.authors: Yeguang Chi; Qionghua (Ruihua) Chu; Wenyan Hao
entries.mechanism: exchange net inflows of BTC, ETH, USDT as intraday return/volatility predictors
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN magnitudes; signs: ETH net inflow negatively predicts ETH returns; USDT net inflow positively predicts BTC and ETH returns; BTC inflow mostly no return predictability (except 4h)
entries.notes: On-chain flow data are paid/vendor (see drafts/ONCHAIN_KILDEAUDIT_2026-10-24.md).

entries.title: Loaded for bear: Bitcoin private wallets, exchange reserves and prices
entries.authors: Lai T. Hoang; Dirk G. Baur
entries.mechanism: exchange reserve changes (wallet <-> exchange transfers) as selling-pressure signal
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: reserve changes negatively related to contemporaneous and future returns; inflows follow large negative shocks)
entries.notes: Data from vendor (CryptoQuant per secondary source). Single asset -> low power.

entries.title: Is Bitcoin Really Untethered?
entries.authors: John M. Griffin; Amin Shams
entries.mechanism: Tether issuance-funded purchases after downturns support BTC prices (supply-based)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract gives no numbers)
entries.notes: Already rejected as candidate in NEXT_MECHANISMS.md row G (episode-specific, one asset).

entries.title: Risk Premia in the Bitcoin Market
entries.authors: Caio Almeida; Maria Grith; Ratmir Miftachov; Zijin Wang
entries.mechanism: option-implied pricing kernel; Bitcoin premium and variance risk premium decomposition; two volatility regimes
entries.market: BTC options (Deribit per search summary) vs S&P 500
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN magnitude; BTC VRP higher than S&P 500; negative returns account for only one-third of the BTC premium; BVRP high in low-vol regime, lower in high-vol regime
entries.notes: Options data not inside current host gates.

entries.title: Net Buying Pressure and the Information in Bitcoin Option Trades
entries.authors: Carol Alexander; Jun Deng; Jianfen Feng; Huning Wan
entries.mechanism: net buying pressure / informed demand vs market-maker limits to arbitrage in Deribit options
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: OTM options carry directional information; ATM driven by volatility traders)

entries.title: A Horserace of Volatility Models for Cryptocurrency: Evidence from Bitcoin Spot and Option Markets
entries.authors: Yeguang Chi; Wenyan Hao
entries.mechanism: GARCH/EGARCH vs historical/EMA volatility forecasts; delta-hedged option trade on GARCH-vs-implied spread
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: GARCH/EGARCH much better; no asymmetric volatility; option strategy reported 'robust profits', no figure)
entries.notes: Profit claim unquantified in abstract; single version, unpublished.

entries.title: Trading and arbitrage in cryptocurrency markets
entries.authors: Igor Makarov; Antoinette Schoar
entries.mechanism: cross-exchange/cross-country price deviations limited by capital controls; signed volume and returns
entries.period: UNKNOWN on page (2017-2018 per paper; not verified)
entries.universe: 34 exchanges in 19 countries (per search summary; not on opened page)
entries.effect_size: common component of signed volume explains 80% of bitcoin returns; deviation sizes UNKNOWN on page
entries.capacity_notes: gaps larger across than within countries -> capital-flow frictions bind
entries.notes: Gaps co-move and widen in bitcoin rallies. Pre-2019 episode.

entries.title: Bitcoin Microstructure and the Kimchi Premium
entries.authors: Kyoung Jin Choi; Alfred Lehar; Ryan Stauffer
entries.venue: working paper, April 2019 version (SNB seminar 31 May 2019)
entries.mechanism: capital controls amplify blockchain-settlement frictions; premium rises with fees, confirmation time, volatility
entries.universe: BTC (premia for LTC, ETH, XRP mentioned per search summary)
entries.effect_size: BTC in Korea on average 4.73% more expensive than in the US
entries.capacity_notes: arbitrage limited by capital controls (KRW conversion)
entries.notes: Premium negatively related to volume. Pre-2018; N4 uses api.upbit.com from 11-14 only.

entries.title: The Kimchi premium and bitcoin-cashing outlets
entries.authors: Jangyoun Lee; Taehee Oh
entries.mechanism: premium linked to cash-out channel (remittances to China) under capital controls
entries.effect_size: premium peaked at 20.8% on 19 May 2021
entries.notes: Uses confidential data on 1,211 FX institutions. Arbitrage requires KRW cash-out we cannot do.

entries.title: The Cross-Section of Cryptocurrency Returns
entries.authors: Nicola Borri; Kirill Shakhnov
entries.mechanism: risk-based explanation of cross-exchange/currency-pair BTC price differences (expensive pairs riskier)
entries.market: BTC across reputable exchanges and fiat pairs
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract has no numbers)
entries.gross_or_net: accounts for transaction costs and trading limits (abstract)
entries.notes: EconPapers subtitle field mentions a high-low bid-ask estimator; counterpoint to pure friction story: premia may be compensation for risk.

entries.title: Building Trust Takes Time: Limits to Arbitrage for Blockchain-Based Assets
entries.authors: Nikolaus Hautsch; Christoph Scheuch; Stefan Voigt
entries.venue: arXiv:1812.00595 (v4 19 Oct 2023); reported as Review of Finance 28(4):1345-1381 (2024) - not opened
entries.mechanism: settlement latency and default risk bound cross-exchange arbitrage
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN on opened page (search snippet of WP version: bounds about 121 bp explaining 91% of differences - NOT verified)

entries.title: BitMEX bitcoin derivatives: Price discovery, informational efficiency, and hedging effectiveness
entries.authors: Carol Alexander; Jaehyuk Choi; Heungju Park; Sungbin Sohn
entries.mechanism: derivatives lead spot in price discovery
entries.market: BitMEX derivatives vs major BTC spot exchanges, minute data
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: BitMEX derivatives lead spot; spreads and relative volumes determine price discovery)
entries.notes: Lab's m21i found weak 'spot leads perp' 1h effect (SCREEN_FAIL); at minute scale the literature says derivatives lead.

entries.title: Forecasting the volatility of Bitcoin: The importance of jumps and structural breaks
entries.authors: Dehua Shen; Andrew Urquhart; Pengfei Wang
entries.mechanism: HAR-RV family with jumps and structural breaks
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN numbers; 18 HAR models; HARQ-F-J best out of sample; structural-break HAR beats no-break at all horizons

entries.title: Cryptocurrency volatility forecasting: What can we learn from the first wave of the COVID-19 outbreak?
entries.authors: Zied Ftiti; Wael Louhichi; Hachmi Ben Ameur
entries.mechanism: HAR extensions: continuous/jump, semivariances, signed jumps
entries.effect_size: best model varies by coin/horizon (MCS 90%); e.g. BTC 1-day MSE 0.00007 full sample; semivariance HAR best OOS
entries.notes: Gains vs plain HAR-RV are model- and regime-dependent; no economic-value test.

entries.title: Risk of Bitcoin Market: Volatility, Jumps, and Forecasts
entries.authors: Junjie Hu; Wolfgang Karl Haerdle; Weiyu Kuo
entries.mechanism: RV with jumps and signed estimators
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: jumps/signed estimators help long-horizon RV forecasts and utility, not short-horizon)
entries.effect_unit_horizon: RV forecast accuracy and utility gain
entries.notes: Positive jumps predict lower future RV.

entries.title: Regime changes in Bitcoin GARCH volatility dynamics
entries.authors: David Ardia; Keven Bluteau; Maxime Rueede
entries.mechanism: Markov-switching GARCH regimes
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: strong evidence of regime changes; MSGARCH beats single-regime for 1-day VaR)
entries.notes: Risk-forecast quality, not return.

entries.title: Forecasting Bitcoin Volatility: A Comparative Analysis of Volatility Approaches
entries.authors: Cristina Chinazzo; Vahidin Jeleskovic
entries.mechanism: historical vs GARCH-type vs option-implied volatility
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: high expected volatility under all methods; thin option liquidity can distort IV)
entries.notes: Weak source; included for IV-quality caveat.
